newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Investors hail steps to prop up Bangladesh shares.
newsitem.headline: Investors hail steps to prop up Bangladesh shares.

text.p: Bangladesh investors and market analysts on Thursday hailed a package of government incentives aimed at reviving the stock market, but said the steps were long overdue.
"The steps are very positive. But it should have been done much earlier to save thousands of investors from losing heavily," said broker Syed Tareque Mohammad Ali.

A Bangladesh Bank (central bank) circular sent to commercial banks on Wednesday asked them to double a credit ceiling to two million taka ($47,000) for small investors and five million taka ($117,000) for licensed brokers.
The banks were also asked to reserve 10 percent of their lending capital for loans to stock investors.

"We are optimistic about the future of the market now. The steps will surely remove any misgivings about the future of the market," central bank governor Lutfar Rahman Sarkar told Reuters on Wednesday.
The news lifted the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE) benchmark index by 4.46 percent to 1,539.7 at the close of Wednesday's trading. The index extended those gains on Thursday.

State-owned Investment Corporation of Bangladesh, the country's only institutional investor, said people would also be able to buy two shares on margin now for every share purchased. The previous ratio was one-for-one.

The market began a heady ascent on anticipated political stability following general elections last June that brought Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to power. Between June and October, the DSE index jumped from less than 1,000 to more than 3,600.

In November, the watchdog Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) imposed a 10-percent limit on daily price movements to check the unbridled rise of share prices. The SEC also warned thousands of new investors against trading in 24 companies with poor financial track records.
The steps triggered panic selling by the investors, dragging the market back down to present levels.
Sarkar said the government would also let merchant banks start operating this month and launch their own mutual funds.
"We are now supporting the market and will continue to do so in future," he said.

Broker Shakil Rizvi said the stock index should hover around 1,700 over the next couple of weeks. "But this may again trigger selling by overseas investors and those who bought shares at high prices, and it will eventually depress the market."
Said broker Khurshid Alam, a former DSE chairman: "The offering of the incentive testifies to the government's positive attitude towards the capital market. It is a very timely decision."
